claims.explanation: Quisinostat (JNJ-26481585) is a pan-HDAC inhibitor whose selectivity is best explained by dependence on HDAC-mediated survival signaling and intact apoptotic/DNA-damage machinery. Lines with TP53 pathway loss, PTEN loss/PI3K-AKT activation, or EGFR/BRAF/NRAS-driven oncogenic signaling appear enriched among sensitive lines, consistent with HDAC inhibition triggering mitochondrial apoptosis and p53 up-acetylation. Conversely, lines with KRAS mutations and/or intact RB1/SMAD4/TGF-beta signaling are enriched among resistant lines, suggesting these pathways buffer HDACi-induced apoptosis.

features.basis: TP53-mutant lines dominate the sensitive set; HDACi induces p53-independent mitochondrial apoptosis
PTEN loss/PI3K-AKT activation enriched in sensitive lines
EGFR-mutant NSCLC lines (NCIH1650, HCC4006, KYSE270) are selectively killed
BRAF-mutant melanoma/colorectal/endometrial lines enriched in sensitive set
NRAS-mutant melanoma and bladder lines appear in sensitive set
ATM-mutant lines enriched among sensitive; HDACi impairs DNA repair
ARID1A-mutant lines (SNUC5, HEC265, KU1919) are selectively killed
KMT2D-mutant lines enriched in sensitive set
KRAS-mutant lines (OV7, T3M4, SNU410, CL11, GSU) are enriched among least affected
RB1-mutant lines appear in resistant set, suggesting intact RB needed for HDACi response
SMAD4-mutant gastric line HGC27 is sensitive, but TGF-beta/SMAD signaling may buffer in resistant lines
Drug is a class I HDAC inhibitor; high HDAC1/2/3 expression predicts target dependence
